definition: The METEO System is a machine translation system specifically designed for the translation of the weather forecasts issued daily by Environment Canada.
details: The system was used from 1981 to 30 September 2001 by Environment Canada to translate forecasts issued in French in the province of Quebec into English and those issued in English in other Canadian provinces into French. Since then, a competitor program has replaced METEO System after an open governmental bid. The system was developed by John Chandioux and was often mentioned as one of the few success stories in the field of machine translation.

explainer.lead: The METEO System translated Environment Canada’s daily weather forecasts between English and French. Its narrow focus on official forecasts made it a notable practical success in machine translation, serving in production from 1981 until 30 September 2001.

tiers.eli5: Imagine a helper whose only job is turning weather reports into another language. METEO took Canadian forecasts written in English or French and produced a version in the other language, so more people could read them. It was specially made for weather forecasts, not for translating every kind of writing.
tiers.practitioner: METEO was applied in Environment Canada’s operational forecast-translation workflow, with the translation direction determined by the forecast’s language and region. Its design centre was a narrow, recurring weather-forecast task rather than general-purpose translation. A replacement selected through an open governmental bid took over after METEO’s service ended on 30 September 2001.
tiers.paperLevel: For an Environment Canada forecast F in English or French, METEO computes T(F), a version in the other language for Canadian forecast distribution. Developed by John Chandioux, it is a domain-specific machine translation system whose documented scope is official daily weather forecasts. Its Canadian production use ended on 30 September 2001.

explainer.example: For a Quebec forecast containing the French phrase “Pluie en matinée,” the translation task is to produce the English forecast phrase “Rain in the morning.”

explainer.intuition: Instead of trying to translate anything, METEO concentrated on one repeated job: converting official Canadian weather forecasts between English and French.
howItWorks: Environment Canada issues a daily weather forecast.
Forecasts issued in French in Quebec are translated into English.
Forecasts issued in English in other Canadian provinces are translated into French.
The translated forecast becomes available in the other official language.
explainer.whyItMatters: METEO supported bilingual weather-forecast distribution in Canada for two decades and was often cited as one of machine translation’s few success stories.
misconceptions: METEO was a weather-forecast translator, not a weather-forecasting system.
It was not a general-purpose translator for arbitrary subjects.
It no longer serves Environment Canada; a competitor replaced it after an open governmental bid.
